questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a trivia interview question and a scenario interview question?
choices: Trivia questions are shorter and faster to ask
Scenario questions test memory; trivia questions test judgment
Trivia questions test recalled knowledge; scenario questions surface how a candidate actually thinks and decides
Scenario questions are only appropriate for senior candidates
questions.explanation: Trivia questions ('what is the difference between X and Y') test whether someone has memorized a definition. Scenario questions ('tell me about a time when...') reveal judgment, priorities, communication choices, and how the person actually behaves — which is what hiring decisions should be based on.

questions.prompt: A recruiter wants to use AI to help screen resumes by pasting candidate applications into ChatGPT. What is the main problem with this approach?
choices: ChatGPT is not capable of reading resume formatting
Candidate names and application materials are PII and should not be entered into a public model without appropriate data agreements
AI will always prefer candidates from top-tier universities
Recruiter screens should only be conducted by phone, not assisted by text analysis
questions.explanation: Candidate resumes contain personally identifiable information. Pasting them into a public AI tool without appropriate data processing agreements violates candidate privacy and may create legal exposure. Only use candidate data in approved tools with proper agreements in place.

questions.prompt: When asking AI to generate interview questions, which prompt instruction produces the most useful output?
choices: Include what a strong answer would address, alongside each question
Specify that questions should be easy enough for an entry-level candidate to answer
Ask for 20 or more questions so there are plenty of options
Avoid mentioning the role level so the questions stay broadly applicable
questions.explanation: Asking AI to include what a strong answer would address gives you a proto-rubric alongside each question. That is the practical tool interviewers need to calibrate their scoring — not just questions in a vacuum.
